question_text: What is the form of government of the United States?
lead_in: You could describe it any of these ways (you only need one):
disambiguation: We most often hear it called a “representative democracy” — the same idea as a “republic”: we elect people to make the laws for us. That's different from a “direct democracy,” where people vote on every law themselves.

why_it_matters.text: In a republic, the power belongs to the people — not a king. We lend it to leaders we elect, and take it back at the next election. In 1787, when kings ruled almost everywhere, trusting regular people to run things was a bold bet.

fun_fact.text: After the Constitutional Convention, someone asked Benjamin Franklin: did we make a republic or a monarchy? “A republic,” he said, “if you can keep it.” His point: this government was brand-new, and keeping it would take work from every generation.
